The City recognizes and appreciates the notable service and valued dining experience that the current Hart House Restaurant operators have provided to Burnaby residents and visitors over many years.
The current lease for the Hart House Restaurant is approaching the end of its term. The City’s standard practice is to publicly advertise lease opportunities for City-owned facilities in order to ensure that public assets are used in the best way possible, for the benefit of Burnaby residents, and that the process is fair and transparent. The current operator, like any interested party, is welcome to participate in the process.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider publicly advertising Hart House Restaurant lease opportunity
agenda_briefs.summary: The City of Burnaby says the current lease for the Hart House Restaurant is nearing the end of its term. Following its standard practice, the City plans to publicly advertise the lease opportunity for this City-owned facility so the process is fair and transparent and the public asset is used in the best way possible. The current operator is welcome to take part in the process like any other interested party. Council has not yet approved how this will proceed, and no new lease terms have been set.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you want to bid on the Hart House Restaurant lease, watch for the City's public advertisement and application details.

agenda_briefs.title: Burnaby to assess LED sign compliance under Sign Bylaw 2026
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby staff are assessing whether a digital LED billboard at 2196 Gilmore Avenue (Gilmore Place, owned by Onni Development) complies with the Burnaby Sign Bylaw 2026. A resident complaint alleges the billboard operates from 05:30 to 23:00, breaking its 23:00–07:00 curfew, and changes images every 7 seconds instead of the required 10-second minimum. Opaque panels removed from a separate light panel also caused white LED light to shine south 24 hours a day toward homes on the 4100 block of Dawson Street. Staff have contacted the property owner; no decision has been made.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you own or operate a digital or illuminated sign in Burnaby, verify it meets the Sign Bylaw 2026 curfew (23:00–07:00), 10-second minimum image display, and brightness rules.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider paid parking expansion at Lake City and Production Way
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a proposal to expand paid parking around the Lake City Way and Production Way–University SkyTrain stations. Staff say these areas have high demand for long-term parking. If approved, the change would mean drivers pay to park in these areas, and staff would watch parking demand and travel patterns after it starts to see if further changes are needed. The proposal ties into Burnaby's Transportation Plan, which aims to make walking, cycling, and transit easier to use.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision — if approved, paid parking could affect your staff, customers, or deliveries in these areas.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider public hearing rules for rezoning applications
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to review how public hearings are handled for rezoning applications under the Local Government Act. Under adopted City policy and Provincial legislation, public hearings are only required for creating or amending an Official Community Plan (OCP), for a rezoning where the proposed use does not fit the existing OCP, or for bylaws tied to a Heritage Revitalization Agreement. Municipalities are not allowed to hold a public hearing when a rezoning is mainly (50% or more) residential, or when creating a Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District. The reasons for skipping a public hearing are currently listed in each rezoning report under Section 4.0 Communication and Community Engagement. Legislative Services also notes that the Additional Information, How to Participate, Submission Deadline and Additional Notice parts of Public Notices are meant to cover all rezoning applications that go to First and Second Readings without a public hearing, and keeping these parts general and consistent avoids errors.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Check whether your rezoning application qualifies for a public hearing — if it is mainly residential or SSMUH, no hearing will be held.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider free mulch and compost program referral
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a proposal to refer the idea of offering free mulch and compost to its Environment Committee for review. The item, brought forward by Tessy Chalissery, would have the committee study whether the city should provide these materials to residents and businesses at no cost. No decision has been made yet — this is only a referral for further discussion, and any program would still need to come back to Council for approval before it could take effect.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider 2026 Pat Quinn Classic Sport Hosting Grant
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider an off-cycle sport hosting grant request for the 2026 Pat Quinn Classic youth hockey tournament, running December 27–31, 2026. The application, submitted by Burnaby Minor Hockey Association, missed the regular grant deadline due to a volunteer's unexpected health circumstances. In 2025 the tournament drew 55 teams (including from the US and Japan), generated over 1,700 Burnaby room nights, and had an estimated $2.1 million economic impact. The item has been referred to the Executive Committee; no funding amount or terms are stated.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Executive Committee meeting date and any chance to speak in support of the grant if your business benefits from tournament traffic.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Burnaby Lake Plan feedback from Horsemen's Association
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider feedback from the Burnaby Horsemen's Association on the draft Burnaby Lake Park Plan, a long-term vision for the Burnaby Lake area. The association's September 11, 2026 letter asks that the lake path west of the power station be formally recognized as part of the horse trails, and notes equestrian trail access in Burnaby has shrunk over the past 20 years. No decisions have been made; comments have been forwarded to senior city staff.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on the draft Burnaby Lake Park Plan — it could affect land use and access near Burnaby Lake.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Williams Lake climate action program funding
agenda_briefs.summary: Williams Lake Council will consider a report on funding from the BC Local Government Climate Action Program. The program provides provincial money to help local governments pay for climate-related projects and planning. Council has not yet decided whether to accept or use the funding. The report is for information only at this stage, so no new rules or fees are being proposed right now. If Council later approves spending the money, it could lead to new climate projects in the city.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to review resident letters on North Burnaby airplane noise
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to receive correspondence from residents about airplane noise over North Burnaby, following new YVR arrival routes implemented under the Vancouver Airspace Modernization Project starting November 2025. One resident at 7444 Government Road reports aircraft passing overhead every five to ten minutes and is asking for an independent post-implementation review measuring actual aircraft frequency, altitude and noise levels, plus permanent noise monitoring in North and Northeast Burnaby. The item is for information only — no vote or new rule is scheduled.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider BEST Mobility active transportation grant program
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a report about the BEST Mobility - BC Active Transportation Infrastructure Grants Program. The BC Active Transportation Infrastructure Grants Program (BCATIG) has been paused for the foreseeable future, and UBCM Resolution EB28 calls on the Province to immediately reinstate it with stable, long-term funding. Council is not voting on a new bylaw or fee, only reviewing the grant program for information. If Burnaby applies and wins grants, road and sidewalk projects could change, which may affect local businesses during construction. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on this grant program — future road and sidewalk projects could affect your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider proposed multiplex at 5512 Buckingham Ave
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a proposed 6-plex at 5512 Buckingham Ave under the province's Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) rules, which allow small apartment-style buildings in areas that previously permitted only single-family homes. The item is on the agenda as a delegation from nearby resident Liang Chen, who is asking Council to enforce strict off-street parking requirements, preserve setbacks and limit site coverage, and complete independent stormwater and sewage capacity assessments before granting permits in established R1 areas. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on this proposal — it could affect what you can build on your property.

agenda_briefs.title: Burnaby Council to review election office accessibility concerns
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is reviewing correspondence from Martin Kendell about accessibility barriers at the temporary Election Office at 6050 Beresford Street. Kendell says the nearest bus stop is a 12-minute walk and the SkyTrain station is a 24-minute walk along a gravel path, and the building has a heavy steel door, concrete steps and a narrow staircase to the second-floor office. He asks that building accessibility be reviewed before the 2030 municipal election, with people with disabilities included in the process. The item is 'for information' — no vote or policy change is proposed.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider study on financial impact of bigger-building rules
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a resident's request to have staff study how the city's small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) rules affected neighbours' property values. The rules allowed four-storey buildings on former single-family lots from 2024 until October 2025, when Council rolled them back to three storeys. The request asks staff to count how many properties are affected and report back before Council decides whether to help owners. No vote has been taken and no new rules are in place.
